corrections_made_during_this_run: the first build's check on GATE 2008's statement item assumed the root of an inorder list must be its median; it need not be, since the left subtree may hold any number of keys. The check was corrected to test what the option actually claims (a sorted list, the key 121 present, and 52 leftmost) and the Examples tab now explains the split at 121 rather than a median

the leaf-range check exposed a real bug in the page's own isLeaf for the 1-based convention: a node j is a leaf when 2j exceeds the largest index n, not when 2j reaches it. Both the check and the helper were fixed
n0 = n2 + 1 was asserted for the empty tree as well, where it is false by one; the identity is now stated for non-empty trees and the exception is named in the detail
two practice items written in the first draft had more than one defensible answer and were rewritten into single-answer items rather than shipped with a caveat

insertion as a failing search, so every new key is a leaf and costs the height
the same six keys in two orders giving heights 2 and 5, with the same inorder both times

the 15-node height pair 3 and 14, with the perfect tree and the chain as the two witnesses

the successor as the leftmost node of the right subtree, or the first ancestor turning right
